Outcome_variable.extract_value: life satisfaction, positive affect, negative affect
Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [016_22_measures] Life satisfaction was assessed using the five-item Satisfaction With Life Scale (SWLS; Diener, Emmons, Larsen, & Griffin, 1985). Participants rated their agreement with statements such as “In most ways my life is close to my ideal” on a 7-point Likert scale ranging from 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree). Higher scores indicate greater life satisfaction. The SWLS demonstrated good internal consistency in the current study (α = .89). Positive and negative affect. Positive and negative affect were assessed using the 20-item Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS; Watson, Clark, & Tellegen, 1988). Participants rated the extent to which they had experienced each of 10 positive affect items (e.g., “interested,” “enthusiastic”) and 10 negative affect items (e.g., “distressed,” “irritable”) during the past week on a 5-point Likert scale ranging from 1 (very slightly or not at all) to 5 (extremely).
